does: Makes fat and a water-based liquid hold together as one smooth sauce, by breaking one into droplets too small to find each other again.
how: Start with the water-based part and whatever helps it hold: egg yolk, mustard, or a liquid boiled down until syrupy.
Add the fat very slowly at first, drop by drop, whisking all the time.
Once the sauce has thickened and holds, add the fat in a thin stream.
Thin it with a few drops of water or acid if it turns stiff and looks oily at the edges.

cues.text: The sauce is smooth, opaque and glossy, and thickens as more fat goes in.
The whisk meets more resistance with every addition.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the fat too fast at the start, so that the sauce stays thin and then separates into oil and liquid.
mistakes.fix: Stop. Start again with a fresh yolk or a spoonful of mustard, and whisk the broken sauce into it drop by drop.

mistakes.mistake: Ingredients at very different temperatures, which makes a cold emulsion refuse to take.
mistakes.fix: Let the egg, the mustard and the oil come to room temperature first.

comes_after.why: An emulsion is whisked the whole time, so a steady whisking hand comes first.
